title: Small Zariski Cech face total site and its canonical module augmentation
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $W:I\to X_{\rm Zar}$ a family of opens, in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]; no covering condition is needed for this definition. The face total site is presented on the tuple-labelled open basis of the levels of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category]: an object is $(n,\mathbf i,V)$ with $\mathbf i:\{0,\ldots,n\}\to I$ and $V\subseteq\bigcap_kW_{i_k}$. A morphism $(n,\mathbf i,V)\to(m,\mathbf j,U)$ is an injective order map $\alpha:[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$ with $i_{\alpha(k)}=j_k$ and $V\subseteq U$. Composition composes these order maps and inclusions. The topology is generated by the vertical families (identity order map, fixed tuple) whose opens cover the target open, using [def-sc-zariski-site]. Thus it is the tuple-labelled open basis of the small Zariski ringed total site for $X_n=\coprod_{\mathbf i\in I^{n+1}}W_{\mathbf i}$, retaining only injective order maps. The forgetful functor $p$ sends $(n,\mathbf i,V)$ to $V$. Given its continuity proof, the ring sheaf is $p^{-1}_{\mathrm{restriction}}\mathcal O_X$, with value $\mathcal O_X(V)$, and $a^*$ on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is actual restriction $G\mapsto((n,\mathbf i,V)\mapsto G(V))$ with the identity scalar map. Let $\operatorname{Augmentation}(W)$ be the proof-only proposition recording continuity of $p$, additivity and exactness of this fixed $a^*$, the existence of its right adjoint, and existence of K-injective resolutions for the total module category. Given such proofs, $a_*$ is the right adjoint fixed by the adjunction universal property, and $Ra_*$ is its ambient K-injective right derived functor on ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The derived adjunction is the canonical one induced by $a^*\dashv a_*$ with exact left adjoint. For $G\in\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, $\operatorname{IsUnitIso}(A,G)$ means that this derived adjunction's unit at $G[0]$ is an isomorphism.
